carousels.name: 4 ways p*rn sites are built to keep you coming back (115M a day)

slides.title: 4 ways p*rn sites are built [[to keep you coming back.]]
slides.sub: 115 million visits a day don't happen by accident.

slides.title: Visits a [[day]]
slides.body: P*rnhub alone reported 42 billion visits in 2019 — about 115 million a day. Sites that big are designed to keep you clicking.

slides.title: Built [[1–2]]
items: Endless free content — no natural stopping point.
Recommendations that push you to something newer, more extreme.

slides.title: Built [[3–4]]
items: Autoplay and previews that pull you into one more.
Private browsing that makes it feel consequence-free.

slides.title: Beat the [[design]]
items: Block p*rn at the device level, not just one browser.
Never "just preview" — previews are the hook.
Know the trick: it's built to keep you, not to help you.
Leave the room when you notice the pull.

carousels.name: 5 reasons you feel worse after p*rn than before

slides.title: 5 reasons you feel worse [[after p*rn than before.]]
slides.sub: The urge promises relief. The after tells the truth.

slides.title: Reasons [[1–2]]
items: Guilt — you broke a promise to yourself.
Tired — it's late and you lost sleep.

slides.title: Reasons [[3–4]]
items: Lonely — p*rn didn't connect you to anyone.
Numb — the feeling you escaped is still there.

slides.title: Time [[gone]]
slides.body: You wanted 10 minutes. You lost an hour. That's the trade p*rn always makes.

slides.title: Next time, [[remember the after]]
items: Write down how you feel after a slip — read it before the next urge.
Ask: what feeling am I trying to fix?
Fix it directly — sleep, call, move, eat.
Be kind to yourself after — then change one thing.
